name: gupnp
desc: Framework for creating UPnP devices and control points
why: A GNOME framework for UPnP devices and control points, opening the protocol from the device side.

brief.what_it_is: GUPnP is an object-oriented open source framework, written in C on GObject and libsoup, for building UPnP devices and control points. The homepage describes it as easy to use, efficient and flexible. Per the archived GNOME wiki, it is one of several libraries: GSSDP handles SSDP discovery and announcement, GUPnP covers announcement, description, control, event notification and presentation, and GUPnP-AV, GUPnP-DLNA and GUPnP-IGD are helper libraries layered on top. The Homebrew formula installs the executable gupnp-binding-tool-1.6. The README does not say what that tool takes in or emits.
brief.why_it_exists: The README frames GUPnP as an easy-to-use, efficient, flexible way to create UPnP devices and control points. The archived wiki adds that it offers the same feature set as libupnp but shields developers from most of UPnP's internals.
brief.how_it_works: The wiki says GUPnP implements the UPnP specification on top of GSSDP for SSDP resource discovery, and includes basic web server functionality through libsoup. It does not include helpers for specific standardized resources such as MediaServer; the wiki says those are left to higher-level libraries. The README itself does not explain the mechanism.

commands_seen.context: From the archived wiki's Development section: clones the latest development version, where PACKAGE_NAME is gssdp, gupnp, gupnp-av, gupnp-tools, gupnp-igd or gupnp-tools. This is a development-source command, not a usage command for the library.

brief.install_notes: The README gives no install steps. The archived wiki says source tarballs are on its Download page and that development happens in the GNOME GitLab repositories. It also says official bindings exist only for Vala, with unofficial PHP bindings and other languages reached through gobject-introspection metadata. The Homebrew formula's executable is gupnp-binding-tool-1.6. Installing the library is therefore a C/GObject build with libsoup and related dependencies, but I did not see the build steps.
brief.standout: Its C code uses GObject and libsoup and is layered as separate libraries for discovery, the core protocol, AV, DLNA and IGD. The wiki says it is written to be used from other languages through gobject-introspection metadata, rather than maintaining a binding for each language.
brief.status: unknown. The GitLab page shows a creation date of May 25, 2018, but no last-release or last-commit date. The wiki page says it has been retired and was last updated 2024-10-23. The wiki points to handbook.gnome.org and gitlab.gnome.org for current information, so the project appears active but I could not confirm it.
brief.caveats: The README is thin and points nowhere useful beyond a changelog and GitLab Pages. The main docs are on gnome.pages.gitlab.gnome.org, which I did not fetch. The archived wiki is retired, so some of its details may be out of date. The project is LGPLv2.1. I saw no usage examples, so I could not confirm what gupnp-binding-tool-1.6 does or what it takes as input.
quotes: GUPnP is an object-oriented open source framework for creating UPnP devices and control points, written in C using GObject and libsoup.
The GUPnP API is intended to be easy to use, efficient and flexible.
GUPnP does not include helpers for construction or control of specific standardized resources (e.g. MediaServer); this is left for higher level libraries utilizing the GUPnP framework.
fetch_log: https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/gupnp - worked; returned page text with the README summary and LGPLv2.1 license, but no install or usage sections
https://wiki.gnome.org/Projects/GUPnP - worked; the page is a retired archive that describes the component libraries, docs links, and development workflow
